newsitem.title: CANADA: Petro-Canada takes hit on oil hedging.
newsitem.headline: Petro-Canada takes hit on oil hedging.

text.p: Petro-Canada said on Thursday that price hedging activities in its upstream division reduced its earnings for the first nine months of 1996 by C$32 million.

Petro-Canada, which said that nine-month earnings rose to C$146 million or C$0.56 a share from C$131 million or C$0.53 a share last year, said it hedged about half its 1996 crude oil and gas liquids production at an average price of US$18.04 a barrel in late 1995.
West Texas Intermediate crude at the time was expected to average between US$16 and US17 a barrel this year, it said.
But WTI has since risen to its highest price levels since the Gulf War in 1991.
"As a result of this hedging program, Petro-Canada's upstream operations have not been able to receive the full benefit of this price increase," the company said.
It said additional opportunity costs, depending on the average crude oil price, were also expected in the fourth quarter.
Petro-Canada said it had no material commodity hedges in place for 1997 and was reviewing its management strategy for price exposure.
